# AI Engineering Compiler v0.5.1

A documentation and test release. Nothing the compiler generates changes, so
there is nothing to re-sync.

## The threat model, after turning the sandbox on

This repository now runs Claude Code's sandbox on itself, and
[`docs/threat-model.md`](https://github.com/akin-oz/ai-engineering/blob/v0.5.1/docs/threat-model.md)
records what that taught:

- **What the sandbox costs.** Its protected paths include `.claude/agents/`
  and `.git/config`, the network starts closed, and SSH agent sockets are out
  of reach. Routine git work (fetch, push, worktrees, signed commits) needs an
  approved unsandboxed retry. The model names the risk that follows: people
  learn to approve retries without reading them.
- **What a pre-allowed host still allows.** Allowing `api.github.com` for `gh`
  also lets a sandboxed command use any GitHub token it holds.
- **A repository's sandbox settings are not always the effective policy.**
  When `network.strictAllowlist` is set in a developer's user, managed, or
  `--settings` settings, Claude Code ignores the repository's `allowedDomains`.
  Narrowing rules still apply. Neither the compiled `.claude/settings.json`
  nor `aie audit` can show the difference.
- **Accepted capability gaps** from 0.5.0 are covered, including
  `accept-unused`.

## Tests

Tests that create commits in temporary repositories now disable commit
signing, so a contributor's signing setup, or a sandbox that blocks its agent,
cannot fail them.
